newsitem.title: USA: Angry John Glenn sees possible funds coverup.
newsitem.headline: Angry John Glenn sees possible funds coverup.

text.p: An angry Democratic Sen. John Glenn charged on Wednesday that Republican leaders would be accused of a "giant coverup" if they refused to let a Senate committee investigate congressional campaign fund wrongdoing.

Glenn, senior Democrat on the Republican-controlled Senate Governmental Affairs committee, urged Republican leaders to run a bipartisan investigation and look not only into Democratic fund raising in the 1996 presidential campaign but also into any improprieties involving Congress.
"It would be looked at like a giant coverup" if the probe were limited to the presidential campaign, the Ohio senator said. "And I think that is absolutely unacceptable."
He said Americans would view that "as a real dodge from investigating the whole problem."
So far, Glenn said, Senate Republican leader Trent Lott wants to confine the probe headed by Tennessee Republican Sen. Fred Thompson to presidential campaign wrongdoing.

Republicans plan to seek Senate Rules Committee approval on Thursday of a $5.7 million budget for the investigation. Democrats want an initial $1.8 million plus agreement that the investigation end this year, inclusion of congressional races and a date for Senate consideration of campaign finance reform legislation opposed by Republican leaders.
Whatever comes out of the rules group would have to be approved by the Senate as well and Democrats may try to block funding if they do not get the scope of the probe widened.
Glenn told a news conference Republicans want to "narrow the focus to only go after the presidential '96 election."
"That means we are trying to sweep this under the table up here," he added. "That means we're not going to look at ourselves up here. We're not really going to look at the problems."

He said "what we're dealing with is more political now -- a Democratic gotcha, and if that is going to be the focus of the hearings, I think it is going to be a very long, tough summer." Democrats favour "cleaning out the stables wherever they need cleaning out," he added.
